ven_001: You can recognise them by the mix of lindens, hackberries and plane trees along both straight avenues and winding paths, over a hundred species in all. They stand in the Giardini della Biennale.
ven_002: You can recognise them by their dark cypress spires rising above the cemetery's brick walls, visible from the water. They stand ringing the Cimitero di San Michele.
ven_004: You can recognise them by the dense green band of cypresses ringing the island, visible from the water around the convent walls. They stand around Isola di San Francesco del Deserto.
ven_007: You can recognise them by the mature planes, holm oaks, cypresses and horse chestnuts shading the garden's terraced paths. They stand in the Giardini Papadopoli, by the train station.
ven_008: You can recognise them by the two hackberries lining the path toward the small Neo-Gothic teatrino. They stand in the Parco di Villa Groggia, Cannaregio.
ven_009: You can recognise them by the row of black locusts leading to the neoclassical loggia, among yews, laurels, cypresses and hackberries. They stand in the garden of Ca' Zenobio degli Armeni.
ven_010: You can recognise them by the large poplars, limes, planes and hackberries planted across the old parade grounds and ramparts. They stand at Forte Marghera, Mestre.
